newsitem.title: USA: U.S. congressional medal proposed for Sinatra.
newsitem.headline: U.S. congressional medal proposed for Sinatra.

text.p: Singer and actor Frank Sinatra would be honoured with a Congressional Gold Medal under a bill introduced on Wednesday.

"Frank Sinatra is one of the all-time greatest entertainers America has ever produced," Senator Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, said in a Senate speech introducing the bill. He said Sinatra had also raised millions of dollars for charities, often anonymously.

"Frank Sinatra is a New Yorker in spirit and soul," D'Amato said. "When he performed 'New York, New York', New Yorkers took a special pride." The singer was born in Hoboken, New Jersey, across the Hudson River from New York City.
D'Amato said he called Sinatra's daughter Nancy on Tuesday night to tell her the bill was being introduced.
"'When I told my father of the efforts being made, he got goosebumps and tears came to his eyes'," D'Amato quoted Nancy Sinatra as telling him.
Sinatra, 81, was released from a hospital in Los Angeles last month after treatment for a heart attack.
D'Amato said his bill had 48 Senate co-sponsors. The bill was also introduced in the House of Representatives by Jose Serrano, a New York Democrat.
